attempts.label: DANDI:000489
attempts.paper_title: Action spectra and mechanisms of (in) efficiency of bipolar electric pulses at electroporation
attempts.entry_title: Bipolar cancellation of electroporation by the second phase amplitude (Kim et al. 2022)
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Kim, Semenov, Kiester, Keppler, Ibey, Bixler and Pakhomov (2022) on dandiset 000489, which holds stitched MemBrite and YO-PRO-1 images of 17 dishes of endothelial cells exposed to unipolar or bipolar 600 ns pulses with a second phase of 25 to 100% (Fig. 2). It measures YO-PRO-1 uptake along the line between the electrodes against the field of a recomputed electrode model, and tests the rise of uptake with field, its exponential slope and the inhibition by the second phase. The experiments of Figs. 3 to 7 and the thermometry are not in the dandiset.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Kim et al. (2022) from dandiset 000489

outcomes.statement: For unipolar 600 ns pulses and for bipolar 600+600 ns pulses with every second phase amplitude, a train of 5 pulses at 1 Hz evoked YP uptake that increased with the local electric field strength.
outcomes.quote: A train of 5 pulses applied at 1 Hz evoked YP uptake proportionally to the local electric field strength ( Fig. 2A ), along with a strong dependence on the 2 nd phase amplitude.
outcomes.notes: Mean YP rises with field for all five amplitudes (Spearman rho 0.98 to 0.99 over 16 ROI from 5.13 to 15.38 kV/cm). Strongest against weakest ROI, YP is higher with p < 0.05 for 50, 75 and 100% under both readings (paired p 0.011, 0.041, 0.003; unpaired p 0.0008, 0.014, below 0.0001) and not for unipolar (2 dishes; paired p 0.17, unpaired p 0.11) or 25% (3 dishes; paired p 0.19, unpaired p 0.15). Paired and unpaired agree on 3 of 5 amplitudes, so the criterion gives partially reproduced. The unipolar test has 2 dishes because the third, sub-Fig2-0-03, holds another dish's YP image. On the top side, with the scale from the electrodes, with the right footprint and with the field scaled to 15.1 kV/cm at the centre the outcome is the same. On the bottom side of bb' alone, or with YP_0 and MB_0 from the left footprint alone, the paired test passes for 2 amplitudes and the unpaired for 3, which the criterion would call methods_underspecified. With the weakest ROI at 2.0 mm (8.14 kV/cm) the outcome is the same; at 2.4 mm (6.75 kV/cm) the paired test passes for 2 and the unpaired for 3.
deviations: The ROI positions are not in the dataset or the paper. 200 um ROI are tiled contiguously along bb' from the midpoint of the electrode centres out to 3 mm, and the two ROI at the same distance are averaged per dish (the claims file's reading a). This is assumed as the reading the paper best supports, since Methods 2.3 and Fig. 1C treat bb' as one line through the centre; one side only is shown for each side.
YP_0 and MB_0 are averaged over discs of 0.5 mm radius in both footprints (Methods 2.5 says "within the electrodes' footprints"); each footprint alone is shown as a variant.

The field per ROI is recomputed from the electrode geometry (Methods 2.3) in closed form for two cylinders in the plane, which gives 15.38 kV/cm at the centre against the 15.1 kV/cm the paper cites. The pixel size, absent from the files, is taken as 0.65 um (6.5 um camera pixel, 10x objective, Methods 2.5); a scale set from each dish's electrode distance is a variant.
Unipolar pulses have 2 dishes, not 3, because sub-Fig2-0-03 is left out (its YP channel is a copy of sub-Fig2-25-04's).

The ROI with the weakest field is the outermost tiled ROI (3.0 mm, 5.13 kV/cm); the paper does not give how far its ROI extend. This is an assumption (bipolar.py, N_ROI_SIDE), and the notebook shows the test with the weakest ROI at 2.0 and 2.4 mm.

(mean plus s.e.m. 785.4), within 1200 and above 250, but the largest 75% mean plus s.e.m. is 283.2 a.u., above the 250 limit (largest mean 239.5). Under every variant of the data the 75% value is 255.2 to 342.8. The ratio of the largest unipolar to the largest 75% mean is 2.38, where the axis limits differ 4.8-fold.
deviations: The files hold uint16 camera counts with conversion 1.0 and unit n.a.; they are assumed to be the units the paper measured in MetaMorph, as nothing in the files or the paper says they were rescaled. Under that assumption the claim is tested on absolute values.
ROI placement, footprints, field and the missing third unipolar dish as for fig2a-uptake-rises-with-field.

outcomes.statement: YP uptake increased exponentially with the field strength, and the second phase did not change the slope of the exponential fits on a semi-log scale.
outcomes.source: Results 3.1, paragraph 1; Figure 2B and its legend
outcomes.quote: YP uptake increased exponentially with the electric field, and the presence of the 2nd phase did not change the apparent slope of exponential fits when plotted on a semi-log scale
outcomes.notes: The criterion calls the claim reproduced when no bipolar slope differs from the unipolar slope at p < 0.05 and the exponential beats a straight line for at least four of five amplitudes, and not reproduced when a slope differs. None of the 12 readings (cutoff 6, 7 or 8 kV/cm; nonlinear least squares or log-linear fit; per-dish slopes or slopes of the fits to the means) meets both parts. In 10 a bipolar slope differs; in the other 2 (least squares with the per-dish test at 7 kV/cm and with the means test at 8 kV/cm) no slope differs but the exponential beats a straight line for only 3 of 5 amplitudes. The exponential is adequate in 2 of 12 readings. Log-linear fits put every bipolar slope below the unipolar one (ratios 0.50 to 0.75; all four differ at p < 0.01 in the means test); least squares gives ratios 0.68 to 1.04. On the bottom side, with the left footprint and with the scaled field every reading also gives not reproduced; on the top side, with the scale from the electrodes and with the right footprint some readings give reproduced, so the outcome rests on the main reading of the ROI, the footprints and the scale. Which fit Grapher made is a question for the paper's authors (findings).
deviations: Log-linear fits drop points with YP at or below zero (2 of 14 unipolar means at the 6 kV/cm cutoff); the count is printed.

A reading in which no slope differs but the exponential is not adequate was labelled partially reproduced in round 1, a category the criterion does not define; it is now not reproduced, as the criterion's reproduced requires both parts.
ROI placement, footprints, field and the missing third unipolar dish as for fig2a-uptake-rises-with-field.

outcomes.statement: The strongest inhibition of YP uptake, to about 20% of the uptake after unipolar pulses, was reached with a second phase of 50 to 75% of the first (p < 0.01).
outcomes.source: Results 3.1, paragraph 2; Figure 2C and its legend
outcomes.quote: The maximum inhibition of YP uptake, down to ~20% of the unipolar pulses, was achieved with the 2 nd phase set to 50-75% of the first one (p<0.01, Fig. 2C ).
outcomes.notes: Over the ROI from 8.94 to 15.24 kV/cm (nearest 8.7 and 15.1), the 50% second phase inhibits most and the lower of 50 and 75% is below 25 and 100% at every ROI, so the ordering holds. The percent of the unipolar mean is 54.5% averaged over the range (reading a, given as measured) and 31.6% at its lowest, at 14.24 kV/cm (reading b), both outside 18 to 22%, so the claim is at most partially reproduced. Where the p < 0.01 test is made is not given; four readings are run. At every ROI of the range it fails for both amplitudes (largest p for 50%, 0.79 against unipolar and 0.072 against 25 and 100%; for 75%, 0.996 and 0.249); on dish means over the range it fails (smallest p 0.011, 50% against 25 and 100%, normalised values); at both named fields it fails (50% against unipolar, p 0.79 at 8.94 and 0.0018 at 15.24 kV/cm). At one ROI or more it holds, 50% against unipolar at 15.24 kV/cm (p 0.0018), the only one of 36 tests (2 amplitudes, 2 comparisons, 9 ROI) below 0.01; that reading would give partially reproduced. At the ROI of strongest inhibition (14.24 kV/cm) p is 0.027 against unipolar and 0.019 against 25 and 100%. With the right footprint alone the pooled test reaches p < 0.01 (partially reproduced); every other variant gives not reproduced under the first three readings. The 100% dishes show more uptake than the unipolar dishes at most ROI (89.6 to 229.9% of unipolar), which the paper does not report.
deviations: Where the p < 0.01 test is made is not given (claims file, criterion; Results 3.1 cites only "Fig. 2C"). It is run at every ROI of the range, on each dish's mean over the range, at both named fields, and at one ROI or more. The outcome assumes the paper's p < 0.01 applies over the range of fields where it reports the inhibition (the first three readings, which agree), not to one ROI chosen from 36 tests; the per-ROI p values are printed.

The range from 8.7 to 15.1 kV/cm is read as the ROI nearest each named field and those between (claims file, opening comment), j 1 to 9; the central ROI (15.38 kV/cm) is above 15.1 in the recomputed field. With the field scaled so that the centre is at 15.1 kV/cm the range starts at the centre ROI, and the mean percent is 52.9%.
ROI placement, footprints, field and the missing third unipolar dish as for fig2a-uptake-rises-with-field.

outcomes.statement: Between 8.7 and 15.1 kV/cm the degree of inhibition by the second phase did not depend on the field strength.
outcomes.quote: The degree of inhibition showed no dependence on the electric field strength between 8.7 and 15.1 kV/cm.
outcomes.notes: The percent of the unipolar mean rises from the ROI at 15.24 to the ROI at 8.94 kV/cm for every amplitude (25%, 76.8 to 199.0; 50%, 34.8 to 113.2; 75%, 42.0 to 155.7; 100%, 133.4 to 229.9). It differs for 50% and 75% under both the paired (p 0.012, 0.049) and the unpaired test (p 0.0016, 0.018), so the criterion gives not reproduced. Of the 36 pairs of ROI in the range, 23 (paired) and 18 (unpaired) differ for 50%. Every variant of the data gives the same outcome. The rise comes from the unipolar mean falling faster with field than the bipolar means in these 2 unipolar dishes (570.4 to 47.7 a.u. over the range).
deviations: ROI placement, footprints, field and the missing third unipolar dish as for fig2a-uptake-rises-with-field.

outcomes.statement: Inhibition was weaker at 6.7 kV/cm than at the higher field strengths, with p < 0.01 for the 50% bipolar pulses and p < 0.05 for the 100% bipolar pulses.
outcomes.quote: However, inhibition was weaker at 6.7 kV/cm (p<0.01 compared to the higher electric field strengths for 50% bipolar pulses, and p<0.05 for 100% bipolar pulses).

statistics.about: 50% bipolar, 6.7 kV/cm against higher field strengths
100% bipolar, 6.7 kV/cm against higher field strengths

outcomes.notes: The criterion divides each bipolar dish by the unipolar mean at the same ROI. At the ROI nearest 6.7 kV/cm (6.75 kV/cm) the unipolar mean YP is -8.6 a.u. with an s.e.m. of 19.6 (the two unipolar dishes give 11.0 and -28.2), not above background, so the percent there (-399% for 50%, -579% for 100%) is a ratio to background and does not measure inhibition. The claim cannot be tested on these two unipolar dishes under the main reading. The unipolar mean is also at background on the top side, with the right footprint, with the scale from the electrodes and with the scaled field. On the bottom side alone (14.8 a.u., s.e.m. 3.3) or with the left footprint alone (7.9 a.u., s.e.m. 3.0) it is more than twice its s.e.m. above zero, and the claim is reproduced under both pairings, with a denominator below 3% of the largest unipolar mean of the main reading (571.1 a.u.). The block thus rests on the main reading of the ROI and the footprints (both sides, both footprints). Dandiset 000548 holds the YP image of the third unipolar dish, 0-03, but it is outside this dandiset and could not be measured as the others are (data check).
deviations: The unipolar mean is taken to be at background when it is not more than twice its s.e.m. above zero (the attempt's rule; in the main reading it is below zero).

ROI placement (both sides averaged) and footprints (both averaged) are the assumptions of fig2a-uptake-rises-with-field; here they decide whether the claim can be tested, and the readings that give reproduced are shown.
The field and the missing third unipolar dish as for fig2a-uptake-rises-with-field.

findings.statement: The dandiset holds only the Fig. 2 experiment (17 dishes, 5 pulses at 1 Hz with a second phase of 0 to 100%) and a sample image named for Fig. 1F. The experiments on pulse number (Fig. 3), pulse duration (Figs. 4 and 5), repetition rate (Fig. 6), the strobe imaging of membrane charging (Fig. 7) and the thermometry (Fig. 1E) are not in it, so 16 of the 22 claims cannot be tested on it. Those of Figs. 3 to 7 are in dandisets 000548, 000549, 000550 and 000448, which name the same paper, but nothing in 000489's metadata or files points to them.

The YP channel of sub-Fig2-0-03 (unipolar) is identical, pixel for pixel in the overview, to the YP channel of sub-Fig2-25-04 (25% bipolar), while their MemBrite channels differ. The YP channel of sub-Fig2-25-04 registers with its own MemBrite channel (phase-correlation peak 0.454) and that of sub-Fig2-0-03 does not (0.028, the level of two unrelated dishes, 0.007 to 0.031). The YP image of unipolar dish 0-03 is missing and replaced by that of dish 25-04, leaving 2 unipolar dishes. Dandiset 000548 holds dish 0-03 as sub-Fig3-Uni5-03, with the same MemBrite channel and a YP channel that registers with it (peak 0.301), so the correct image exists in another dandiset.
The file sub-Fig1F holds the same image in both channels, although its series is described as two channels (MemBrite and YO-PRO-1).

Each stitched two-channel image is stored as an ImageSeries with data of shape (22323, 22323, 2) and a starting_time rate of 2 Hz. As an ImageSeries the first axis is time, so the file reads as 22323 frames of 22323 x 2 pixels; an Images container with two GrayscaleImage objects, or a series of shape (1, 22323, 22323) per channel, would describe it. The unit is n.a. and the three 25% files share the acquisition name Fig2_25.

The files give no pixel size, electrode positions, ROI, field per ROI, footprint values (YP_0, MB_0) or pulse voltage, and identify the channels only in free text. Everything the paper plots has to be remeasured from the images, and the field recomputed from the paper's geometry. The data are consistent with 0.65 um per pixel (electrode centres 4.54 mm apart, footprints 1.49 mm across, against 4.5 and 1.5 mm in the paper).

The series description says the image was stitched from 144 images (12 x 12) of "a whole well from a six-well plate"; the paper says 216 images of cells in 35 mm glass-bottom dishes (Methods 2.1 and 2.5). The images show a 12 x 12 tile grid over a round glass bottom about 14.5 mm across.

Dish numbers in the subject ids run up to 18 (sub-Fig2-50-18), so more dishes were exposed than deposited, and nothing says which dishes form Fig. 2. All unipolar dishes are from 2021-07-29 and all 75% and 100% dishes from 2021-08-24, a day with no unipolar dish. In these files the 100% dishes show more uptake than the unipolar ones (largest mean 761.0 against 571.1 a.u.), which does not match Fig. 2C, where every second phase inhibits uptake.

Questions for the paper's authors. (1) How were the 200 um ROI placed along bb' (the spacing, how far out, whether both sides of the centre were measured and averaged)? With the two sides averaged, the unipolar mean at 6.7 kV/cm is at background and fig2c-weaker-at-6-7 cannot be tested; with the bottom side alone it is reproduced. (2) Were YP_0 and MB_0 taken from both electrode footprints or one, and over what area? With the left footprint alone fig2c-weaker-at-6-7 is reproduced. (3) Were the exponential fits of Fig. 2B made by nonlinear least squares or on log values, to means or to dish values, and from which field? The slope comparison depends on it. (4) Were the t-tests paired across ROI of the same dish, and for Fig. 2C which groups and which fields does p < 0.01 compare? At one ROI (15.24 kV/cm) 50% differs from unipolar at p < 0.01; over the range it does not. (5) Were the field values of the ROI taken from the Sim4Life model at nominal electrode positions, or adjusted per dish? The recomputed centre field is 15.38 kV/cm against the cited 15.1.

disagreements.reason: 10 of 12 readings have a bipolar slope that differs from unipolar at p < 0.05. Slopes for 50% and 75% are 0.68 to 0.72 of unipolar (NLS) or 0.50 to 0.59 (log). The other 2 readings have the exponential beating a straight line for only 3 of 5 amplitudes, so the criterion's reproduced fails there too. The notebook labels "no slope differs, exponential not adequate" as partially_reproduced, a category the criterion does not define, and that label is the only source of the disagreement between readings that yields methods_underspecified. Read against the criterion, all 12 readings fail.

The unipolar mean at 6.75 kV/cm is -8.6 a.u. (dishes at 11 and -28), so the percent of unipolar is -399% (50%) and -579% (100%). That is a ratio to background, not a measure of inhibition. The code divides by a unipolar mean that is at or below background and never flags it; whether the test passes depends on the sign of a near-zero denominator. The outcome flips to reproduced on the bottom side and with the left footprint alone, where this denominator changes. (Blocked, other.)

entries.name: 000489-kim-2022
entries.title: Bipolar cancellation of electroporation by the second phase amplitude (Kim et al. 2022)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Kim, Semenov, Kiester, Keppler, Ibey, Bixler and Pakhomov (2022) on dandiset 000489, which holds stitched MemBrite and YO-PRO-1 images of 17 dishes of endothelial cells exposed to unipolar or bipolar 600 ns pulses with a second phase of 25 to 100% (Fig. 2). It measures YO-PRO-1 uptake along the line between the electrodes against the field of a recomputed electrode model, and tests the rise of uptake with field, its exponential slope and the inhibition by the second phase. The experiments of Figs. 3 to 7 and the thermometry are not in the dandiset.
